## Case studies

Five published, all real client work. Timelines across all five: 8–12 weeks (two at 8 weeks, two at 10 weeks, one at 12 weeks).

### FinPilot — Autonomous Finance Ops for a 65-Person Creative Agency
Client: NorthBridge Studios. Engagement: Agentic AI system. Timeline: 8 weeks, Q1 2025. Status: Live — fully autonomous.
Five agentic workflows replacing two weeks of monthly finance work — invoice processing, AP/AR reconciliation, and reporting, with human approval gates.
Results: monthly close time 9 days → 2 days; invoice processing cost $14 → $2 each; days to collect payment 47 → 28; weekly reconciliation hours 22 → 4.
URL: https://theboatgrp.com/work/finpilot

### Bounce — Court Booking App for Players & Operators
Client: Bounce Sports, Colombo. Engagement: Mobile app + admin dashboard. Timeline: 10 weeks, Q2–Q3 2025. Status: In development.
Real-time availability, instant confirmation, and a full operator management system for sports facility operators.
Results: one mobile app + one admin dashboard on a shared API; under 3 minutes from opening the app to a confirmed, paid booking; 0 double-bookings via real-time slot locking.
URL: https://theboatgrp.com/work/bounce

### Hima Products — 30 Animal Feeders, One Online Store
Client: Hima Products, a Sri Lankan animal feeder company. Engagement: Product website + online store. Timeline: 8 weeks, Q1 2025. Status: Live.
Spec-first product pages and direct-to-customer checkout, replacing phone and WhatsApp orders.
Results: 30+ products live and filterable across 3 categories (pet feeders, farm & livestock feeders, accessories); direct-to-customer ordering enabled for the first time, no dealer required.
URL: https://theboatgrp.com/work/hima

### Troi — Real-Time ROAS & ROI Analytics for SME Marketing Teams
Client: Troi, Colombo. Engagement: SaaS dashboard. Timeline: 12 weeks, Q1–Q2 2025. Status: Beta.
Marketing analytics dashboard giving SME teams real-time ROAS and ROI across every ad channel, against actual store sales rather than platform-reported numbers.
Results: 4+ channels (Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok, email) unified into one attribution view; continuous spend/sales sync, no waiting for end-of-month reports; replaces four ad-platform tabs and a Shopify reports page with a single dashboard.
URL: https://theboatgrp.com/work/troi

### OLYCE — Luxury Sri Lanka Tour Booking Website
Client: OLYCE, Colombo. Engagement: Luxury tour booking website. Timeline: 10 weeks, Q2–Q3 2025. Status: Live.
Editorial photography up front, full 7-day itineraries before the inquiry, Standard vs Premium pricing side-by-side.
Results: 4 tour packages live with full itineraries (Cultural Heritage, Hill Country, South Coast Beaches, Wildlife & Safari), starting from $480/person; 2 pricing tiers surfaced on every package page; all site journeys converge on a single Inquire CTA.
URL: https://theboatgrp.com/work/olyce

## Tools & stack

As named on the site: n8n, Make, Claude, OpenAI (automation); Shopify, Klaviyo, Stripe, Aramex (commerce); Notion, Airtable, HubSpot (ops); Next.js, React, TypeScript, Supabase, Vercel (product).

## How engagements work

Starts with a discovery call and a 48-hour blueprint. Product builds run milestone-by-milestone with daily communication. Automation projects are scoped upfront (usually $15,000–$40,000) with the option to keep iterating on retainer. There's a stabilisation window after every launch. Everything is documented and handed over — code, accounts, configs, docs — no lock-in.

## FAQ

### Do you build products or just automate workflows?
Both. theBOAT works with early-stage founders who need a team to build their product — usually 8-week sprints from idea to shipped. It also works with growing teams drowning in manual ops who need those hours back. Same approach, different problems.

### What does a typical engagement look like?
It starts with a discovery call and a 48-hour blueprint. From there, product builds run milestone-by-milestone with daily comms. Automation projects are scoped upfront (usually $15k–40k) with the option to keep iterating on retainer.

### What makes theBOAT different?
theBOAT pushes back — it doesn't just take a brief and disappear, it flags when an approach looks wrong and explains why. It's opinionated about what AI automation should do: agents that act on real ops (inventory, pricing, document flows), not chatbots that answer FAQ questions.

### What about support after the project ends?
There's always a stabilisation window after launch. Automation clients can stay on retainer for new flows and iteration as the business grows. Everything is documented and handed over if a client wants to move the system elsewhere.

### Which tools and stack does theBOAT work with?
Automation: n8n, Make, Claude, OpenAI. Commerce: Shopify, Klaviyo, Stripe, Aramex. Ops: Notion, Airtable, HubSpot. Product: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Supabase, Vercel. If it has an API, it can probably be connected.
